Referred to as the "**King of Rock and Roll**", he is widely regarded as [one of the most culturally significant figures of the 20th century](/wiki/Cultural_impact_of_Elvis_Presley "Cultural impact of Elvis Presley"). He began his music career in 1954 at [Sun Records](/wiki/Sun_Records "Sun Records") with producer [Sam Phillips](/wiki/Sam_Phillips "Sam Phillips"), who wanted to bring the sound of [African-American music](/wiki/African-American_music "African-American music") to a wider audience. Presley, on guitar and accompanied by lead guitarist [Scotty Moore](/wiki/Scotty_Moore "Scotty Moore") and bassist [Bill Black](/wiki/Bill_Black "Bill Black"), was a pioneer of [rockabilly](/wiki/Rockabilly "Rockabilly"), an uptempo, [backbeat](/wiki/Backbeat_(music) "Backbeat (music)")-driven fusion of [country music](/wiki/Country_music "Country music") and [rhythm and blues](/wiki/Rhythm_and_blues "Rhythm and blues"). In 2023, Patty Murray became the first woman to serve as [president pro tempore](/wiki/President_pro_tempore_of_the_United_States_Senate "President pro tempore of the United States Senate"), a role traditionally given to the most senior member of the majority party in the United States Senate. Dianne Feinstein was the most senior Democratic senator but declined to serve. This made Murray the third person [in line](/wiki/United_States_presidential_line_of_succession "United States presidential line of succession") to become president, after the [vice president](/wiki/Vice_President_of_the_United_States "Vice President of the United States") and the [Speaker of the House](/wiki/Speaker_of_the_United_States_House_of_Representatives "Speaker of the United States House of Representatives").[[14]](#cite_note-16)

As of 2025, 64 women have served in the United States Senate since its establishment in 1789.[[15]](#cite_note-17) Cumulatively, 39 female U.S. senators have been Democrats, while 26 have been Republicans and one is an independent. As of 2023, no female U.S. senator has ever won election to the House after her Senate term, resigned from a state governorship for the purpose of a Senate appointment by her successor, also won election as an independent or to represent more than one state in non-consecutive elections, served both seats of a state at different times, or represented a [third party](/wiki/Third_party_(U.S._politics) "Third party (U.S. politics)") in her career. In December 2022, Senator Kyrsten Sinema became the first female senator to switch her party affiliation while in office. In September 2023, Senator Dianne Feinstein became the first female senator to die in office.

Some female U.S. senators have later run for U.S. president or vice president (see [list of female United States presidential and vice presidential candidates](/wiki/List_of_female_United_States_presidential_and_vice_presidential_candidates "List of female United States presidential and vice presidential candidates")). LeBlanc found success as the dimwitted but lovable [Joey Tribbiani](/wiki/Joey_Tribbiani "Joey Tribbiani") on *[Friends](/wiki/Friends "Friends")*; he played this character for 12 years—10 seasons of *Friends* and two seasons of [*Joey*](/wiki/Joey_(TV_series) "Joey (TV series)"). *Friends* was wildly successful, and LeBlanc (along with co-stars [Jennifer Aniston](/wiki/Jennifer_Aniston "Jennifer Aniston"), [Courteney Cox](/wiki/Courteney_Cox "Courteney Cox"), [Lisa Kudrow](/wiki/Lisa_Kudrow "Lisa Kudrow"), [Matthew Perry](/wiki/Matthew_Perry "Matthew Perry"), and [David Schwimmer](/wiki/David_Schwimmer "David Schwimmer")) gained wide recognition among viewers. This ensemble situation comedy became a major hit for NBC, airing on Thursday nights for ten years.

For his performance, LeBlanc received three [Primetime Emmy Award](/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award "Primetime Emmy Award") nominations, three [Golden Globe](/wiki/Golden_Globe "Golden Globe") award nominations, and one [Screen Actors Guild Award](/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award "Screen Actors Guild Award") nomination. During this time he also appeared in the films *[Lookin' Italian](/wiki/Lookin%27_Italian "Lookin' Italian")* (1994), *[Ed](/wiki/Ed_(film) "Ed (film)")* (1996), *[Lost in Space](/wiki/Lost_in_Space_(film) "Lost in Space (film)")* (1998), *[Charlie's Angels](/wiki/Charlie%27s_Angels_(2000_film) "Charlie's Angels (2000 film)")* (2000), and its sequel, *[Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle](/wiki/Charlie%27s_Angels:_Full_Throttle "Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle")* (2003).

Following the cancellation of *Joey*, LeBlanc announced that he would be taking a one-year hiatus from acting on television, which eventually turned into five years.[[11]](#cite_note-11)

Haroche, who won Nobel Prize in Physics in 2012, visited Stockholm, June 2016, as a member of the Wallenberg Foundation Scientific Advisory Board.

Haroche works primarily in [atomic physics](/wiki/Atomic_physics "Atomic physics") and [quantum optics](/wiki/Quantum_optics "Quantum optics").[[16]](#cite_note-16)[[17]](#cite_note-17)[[18]](#cite_note-18)[[19]](#cite_note-19)[[20]](#cite_note-20)[[21]](#cite_note-21)[[22]](#cite_note-22) He is principally known for showing [quantum decoherence](/wiki/Quantum_decoherence "Quantum decoherence") by experimental observation, while working with colleagues at the École normale supérieure in Paris in 1996.

After a [PhD](/wiki/PhD "PhD") dissertation on dressed atoms under the supervision of [Claude Cohen-Tannoudji](/wiki/Claude_Cohen-Tannoudji "Claude Cohen-Tannoudji") (who would receive the 1997 Nobel Prize) from 1967 to 1971, he developed new methods for [laser spectroscopy](/wiki/Laser_spectroscopy "Laser spectroscopy"), based on the study of [quantum beats](/wiki/Quantum_beats "Quantum beats") and [superradiance](/wiki/Superradiance "Superradiance"). He then moved on to [Rydberg atoms](/wiki/Rydberg_atom "Rydberg atom"), giant atomic states particularly sensitive to [microwaves](/wiki/Microwave "Microwave"), which makes them well adapted for studying the interactions between light and matter. He showed that such atoms, coupled to a [superconducting](/wiki/Superconductivity "Superconductivity") cavity containing a few [photons](/wiki/Photon "Photon"), are well-suited to the testing of [quantum decoherence](/wiki/Quantum_decoherence "Quantum decoherence") and to the realization of [quantum logic](/wiki/Quantum_logic "Quantum logic") operations necessary for the treatment of [quantum information](/wiki/Quantum_information "Quantum information").
